newsitem.title: USA: Prosecutors will seek death penalty for Penn State shooter.
newsitem.headline: Prosecutors will seek death penalty for Penn State shooter.

text.p: A 19-year-old woman who once served in the Army reserve was charged with murder on Wednesday for a shooting on the Penn State campus and prosecutors said they would seek the death penalty.

Jillian Robbins, 19, was charged with firing five shots from a high-powered rifle, killing Melanie Spalla, 19, and wounding Nicholas Mensah, 22. Robbins is not a Penn State student and said she did not know the people she shot.
Centre County District Attorney Ray Gricar said Robbins told authorities she "just decided to shoot" when asked why she shot at the students.

Police said she may have planned the crime a month ago. "She had spoken to acquaintances (a month ago) about 'doing it'," said Dave Stormer, assistant vice president for university safety. "We are speculating that 'it' may be (the shooting)."
Robbins was listed in fair condition at Centre Community Hospital, where she underwent surgery Tuesday for a self-inflicted stab wound.
Students said they were trying to get back to normal a day later.
"I think people are just trying to get things back to normal," said James Reeser, 22. "You try to forget it ... but you can't.
"People are walking by the spot where it happened and some won't look at it. It's like they stare straight ahead, trying not to look," he said.

Stormer said Robbins had been in an Army Reserve unit and that dog tags were strapped to the 7 mm Mauser rifle they found at the scene. A background search produced no criminal record and a search of her apartment produced "nothing significant," he added.
Stormer said several people saw Robbins sitting outside near the school's student centre reading a newspaper early Tuesday. She was then seen hiding beneath a tree before opening fire.

One student's life was saved when one of the bullets struck the student's backpack, Stormer said. Mensah, who suffered a wound to the abdominal area, was listed in fair condition at Centre Community Hospital.
Police said that after shooting the two students, Robbins stopped to reload the rifle and was tackled by another student. She tried to stab the student but missed and struck her own leg.
